name: Design Craft Rulebook
summary: Small decisions that separate a considered design from a template.
check: Squint at each page: one focal point, one primary action.
List every distinct spacing, radius and colour value in the CSS; anything not a token is a fix.

rules.title: Delete filler badges
rules.text: Remove any badge, chip or label that does not carry information.

rules.title: Drop redundant labels
rules.text: No "Email:" above a field whose placeholder is already an email. No "Our Services" above three service cards. If the content says it, the label does not need to.

rules.title: Unitalicize random words
rules.text: Italics only for titles of works, foreign words or one deliberate emphasis.

rules.title: Mono only where needed
rules.text: Numbers that change or align (prices, timers, tables), codes, IDs.

rules.title: Use a design system
rules.text: Define tokens before building: colour, type scale (about 5–7 sizes), spacing scale (for example 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96), radii, shadows, motion durations. Never invent a one-off value.

rules.title: Show the actual product
rules.text: Real screenshots, real photos, real UI. Mockups only of the real thing.

rules.title: Enlarge the main feature
rules.text: The most important thing on each page is clearly the biggest. Hierarchy is readable at a glance.

rules.title: Group with spacing
rules.text: Related items sit closer together, groups sit further apart. Spacing does the grouping before any border or background.

rules.title: Make headlines specific
rules.text: "Invoices sent in 30 seconds" beats "Revolutionise your finances".

rules.title: Emphasise the CTA
rules.text: One primary action per view, visually the strongest element. Secondary actions look secondary.

rules.title: One accent colour, used sparingly
rules.text: For the primary button, links and key highlights only.

rules.title: Keep icons consistent
rules.text: One set, one stroke width, one size grid, one corner style.

rules.title: Remove embellishments
rules.text: Ornaments, extra gradients and decorative shapes that say nothing go.

rules.title: Inner radius = outer radius − padding
rules.text: A card with 20 px radius and 8 px padding holds children with 12 px radius. Nested corners then look concentric.

rules.title: Text contrast
rules.text: WCAG AA at least: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI parts. Check muted text and dark mode especially.

rules.title: Wrap headlines properly
rules.text: `text-wrap: balance` on headings, `text-wrap: pretty` on paragraphs. No single orphaned word on the last line. Set a sensible max width (about 60–75 characters for body text).

rules.title: Align by eye, not by pixels
rules.text: Optically centre play triangles, arrows and round icons. Nudge icons next to text to sit on the visual centre line.

rules.title: Tabular numbers
rules.text: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for prices, timers, counters and table columns, so digits do not jump.

rules.title: Loading states everywhere
rules.text: Every action and every data region has a loading state that matches the final layout (`ST-02`).

rules.title: Animate useful feedback
rules.text: Animation confirms something happened (added to bag, saved, error). It is never only decoration.

rules.title: One radius scale
rules.text: Corners come from a small radius scale (for example 4, 8, 12, 999). Every card, button and input uses it, and nested corners stay concentric (`DC-14`).

rules.title: Every interactive element looks interactive
rules.text: Cards that link have a hover and focus state, a cursor change and a clear target; static cards do not pretend to be clickable.

rules.title: Optical sizes for icons
rules.text: Icons sit on a fixed size grid (16, 20, 24) with one stroke width, and are visually balanced against the cap height of the text next to them.

rules.title: Decoration that competes with content
rules.text: No ornament, shape or effect draws the eye before the headline, the product or the action. If people remember the decoration first, remove it.

rules.title: One-off values
rules.text: No spacing, colour, radius, shadow or font size that is not a token. A one-off value is a missing token or a mistake (`DC-05`).

rules.title: Shadows fall on open ground, never through houses
rules.text: In an architectural or product scene a shadow lands only where something could receive it. Mask the shadow-catching ground inside every footprint, so a shadow stops at the edge of a building instead of showing through it. See-through volumes do not receive shadows, and their sunlit walls must never be brighter than the shade behind them (cap their colour), or a shadow seen through a wall turns into a white patch. Every shadow starts at the foot of what casts it; a gap means the shadow map is stale or biased.
